get.description:
No side effect, no token minted — a caller can fetch this as many
times as it likes while the human is still reading.

post.description:
Mints the one-shot token `run_all` requires. Always recomputes the
spec itself rather than trusting anything the caller might send —
`mint_confirmation` is issued only after *this* call has the spec in
hand (D31).

`"start"` has nothing real to start under the `nbclient` fallback —
there is no persistent per-experiment kernel (D30's descope) — so it
just reports current status, same as a bare query would.
`"stop"` is real: it cancels this experiment's in-flight run container,
if any (`sandbox.stop_kernel`).

Dispatches the run via Job Queue rather than awaiting it inline —
the container execution can run long, and cancellation/log streaming
already ride the job/WS pipes independently of this request. The
`run_id` is assigned here so the client has a stable id to correlate
against `run_log`/`run_status` events on the project's WebSocket before
the run itself has produced anything.

get.description:
A plain-text response is enough for now: the captured stdout of one
notebook run is bounded by the sandbox's own cell/idle timeouts, not an
arbitrarily large stream — unlike a paper PDF (`GET /api/papers/:id/pdf`,
which streams via `FileResponse` because PDFs can be large binaries),
there is no comparable size case here yet. If run logs grow large enough
to matter, this is the seam to swap for a streaming response.

schema.title: Response List Project Papers Api Projects  Project Id  Papers Get

AnchorHint.title: AnchorHint
AnchorHint.description: A cached rendering hint only — never identity (TRD §4.1).

CitedRow.title: CitedRow
CitedRow.description:
One retrieval hit, always traceable back to the row it came from
(MODULES.md `query_memory`) — the paper it's from when it has one, the
verbatim text, and the span within the source artifact.

ConfirmationToken.title: ConfirmationToken
ConfirmationToken.description:
The one-shot credential `run_all` requires (D31) — opaque beyond the
fields the approval prompt needs to display (`expires_at`, for a
countdown or a "this approval expired, review again" message).

Experiment.title: Experiment
Experiment.description: The `experiments` row (Schema.md), returned by every experiments endpoint.

ExperimentInput.title: ExperimentInput
ExperimentInput.description:
What a caller submits to create or update an experiment record.

All fields are optional so `update_experiment` can patch just one; on
create, `title` is the only one that must be present in practice — the
module enforces that, not this shape.

ExperimentMetric.title: ExperimentMetric
ExperimentMetric.description: The `experiment_metrics` row (Schema.md), returned by the metrics endpoint.

ExperimentRun.title: ExperimentRun
ExperimentRun.description:
The `experiment_runs` row (Schema.md) — the strongest provenance in
the system. `approved_at` is always set: a row cannot exist without a
validated confirmation token (D31, invariant #5). This is the type
`record_run` returns and `is_measured_eligible` inspects; Execution
Sandbox re-exports it (`sandbox.models.ExperimentRun`) rather than
defining a second, duplicate shape, since Experiment Record is the
module that persists this row (MODULES.md's own `record_run` signature).

Highlight.title: Highlight
Highlight.description: The `highlights` row (Schema.md), returned by the highlights endpoint.

KernelStatus.title: KernelStatus
KernelStatus.description:
Response for `POST /api/experiments/:id/kernel`. Under the `nbclient`
fallback (D30's descope) there is no persistent per-experiment kernel to
start or stop — containers are per-run, not per-experiment. `state`
honestly reports the only kernel-shaped fact that exists here: whether
this experiment currently has an in-flight run container. `"start"`
cannot create anything real to report back beyond this same status;
`"stop"` maps to cancelling that in-flight container, if any.

MetricInput.title: MetricInput
MetricInput.description:
What a caller submits to `record_metric`. `source: llm` is
unrepresentable at the type level (`MetricSource`); `run_id` is required
by the caller only when `source='measured'` — the DB `CHECK` is what
actually enforces that pairing (MODULES.md), this shape just allows it.

MountSpec.title: MountSpec
MountSpec.description:
One bind mount into the run container (D30/Rules.md: never the whole
vault, never `$HOME`).

Note.title: Note
Note.description: The `notes` row (Schema.md), returned by every notes endpoint.

NoteInput.title: NoteInput
NoteInput.description:
What a caller submits to create or update a note.

`frontmatter_id` is absent to create (Vault Writer assigns one) and
present to update — the id carried in the note's own YAML frontmatter,
never the file path (D4).

Notebook.title: Notebook
Notebook.description: The vault notebook's cell list, returned by `propose_cell`.

NotebookCell.title: NotebookCell
NotebookCell.description:
One cell as the UI needs to render it. `execution_count` and
`outputs` absent/empty is the unrun signal `propose_cell` relies on —
nbformat's own freshly-created code cell already carries no other kind
of "pending approval" marker, so none is invented here (MODULES.md).

PaperInput.title: PaperInput
PaperInput.description:
What the caller submits to add a paper — from a search result or a
pasted link/id. A pure upload with no resolvable id is out of scope for
v1: `canonical_id_source` (Schema.md) has no "upload" value, so at least
one of doi/arxiv_id/openalex_id/s2_id is required.

ProviderCredentials.title: ProviderCredentials
ProviderCredentials.description: What the user submits to save and validate one provider.

ProviderInfo.title: ProviderInfo
ProviderInfo.description: What is ever read back — never ciphertext, nonce, or plaintext key.

QuoteAnchorInput.title: QuoteAnchorInput
QuoteAnchorInput.description:
The wire shape of `QuoteAnchor` in TRD §4.1 — what a caller submits
to be validated and anchored fresh (D24), same as an extractive card
field.

RunDetail.title: RunDetail
RunDetail.description:
`ExperimentRun` plus the run's captured stdout log content — the log
itself lives on disk (`stdout_ref` is a vault-relative path), so this
reads it back rather than making the caller resolve the path itself.

RunSpec.title: RunSpec
RunSpec.description:
The container spec the approval prompt displays before `run_all` can
mint a confirmation (D31) — image, mounts, network, and the limits that
are "always set" per Rules.md's Security Rules. Nothing in Phase 2.1
consumes this yet; `mint_confirmation`/`run_all` (Phase 2.2) do.

RunSpecPreview.title: RunSpecPreview
RunSpecPreview.description:
What the approval prompt renders before a human confirms: the
proposed code and the full container spec (image, mounts, network,
GPU) — D31's explicit requirement for what the prompt must show.

SourceIds.title: SourceIds
SourceIds.description: Whatever source ids a literature API returned for one paper.

TabRef.title: TabRef
TabRef.description:
One entry in the persisted center-pane tab stack (TRD §4.1's
`TabRef`) — a routed view instance, e.g. two open papers are two
entries with the same `kind` and different `params`.
